items.title: Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals
items.content:
Bitcoin miners face widening AI financing costs as lenders scrutinize deals
The Bitcoin mining industry needs roughly $50 billion to complete planned AI infrastructure projects, with IREN, Riot Platforms and HIVE Digital facing major funding gaps.
Bitcoin mining companies expanding into artificial intelligence and high-performance computing face sharply different borrowing costs as lenders scrutinize large-scale data center projects, adding to the industry’s growing financing challenges.
According to the latest Miner Weekly newsletter from BlocksBridge Consulting, securing major AI customers has only been part of the challenge for miners. Companies must also raise billions of dollars to purchase computing equipment, build facilities and secure the power infrastructure needed to fulfill their contracts.
“[B]ig lenders have become more selective about data center loans and decisions increasingly depend on the customer, the contract and the path to completion,” BlocksBridge said.
IREN, which has expanded from Bitcoin mining into AI infrastructure, illustrates the differences in financing costs. The company secured a $3.65 billion GPU financing package in June at a blended interest rate of 6%, followed by a separate $2.4 billion financing arrangement in August at a fixed rate of 9%. The two agreements cover different projects, so they’re not directly comparable, but they show how borrowing costs can vary even within the same company.
Financing arrangements can also carry costs beyond interest payments. In a separate transaction involving Cipher Digital, Google agreed to backstop $1.4 billion in lease obligations in exchange for warrants representing 5.4% of Cipher’s equity, subject to certain adjustments. Exercising those warrants could dilute existing shareholders.
The financing requirements highlight a broader challenge for Bitcoin miners entering the AI market. Even companies with multibillion-dollar customer contracts may need substantial additional capital before their data centers become operational.
Related: Hut 8, IREN deals lift AI-focused Bitcoin mining stocks
Bitcoin miners face massive AI funding gap
The differences in financing costs come as Bitcoin miners take on billions of dollars in debt to fund their AI expansion plans. At the height of the Bitcoin bull market last October, VanEck data showed that miners’ debt had surged roughly 500% from the second quarter of 2024.
Ironically, capital requirements have continued to grow during the Bitcoin bear market as miners shift away from BTC mining amid deteriorating economics. A June 2026 analysis by BlocksBridge Consulting, citing VanEck data, estimated that publicly traded Bitcoin miners needed roughly $50 billion to complete their planned AI infrastructure projects, including a $21.1 billion funding gap at IREN alone.
Riot Platforms and HIVE Digital also face substantial funding requirements, estimated at $7.2 billion and $4.6 billion, respectively.
Related: Crypto Biz: Wealthy investors are buying crypto, but their advisers aren’t sold

items.title: Bitcoin Spooked? Crypto Fear and Greed Index Drops to Pre-Rally August Lows
items.content:
In brief
- The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 56 (neutral) on Monday from 67 a week earlier and an Aug. 26 peak of 82, the highest reading of the year.
- Bitcoin dropped about 6%, from $86,978 to $81,749.83, as oil topped $101, the 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.70% and spot.
- Myriad traders now give 45% odds of Biticoin hitting $87,500 and 56% odds of BTC dropping to $80,000 in October, both lower than on Oct. 7.
After a red hot summer lifted Bitcoin and the rest of crypto out of a brutal bear market, sentiment has now clearly shifted, bucking typically reliable seasonal trends.
Bitcoin is now trading just above $82,000, down close to 5% for the week, and the cryptocurrency market’s Fear and Greed Index fell to 56 on Monday, a “neutral” reading, after reaching “extreme greed” in late August.
The Fear and Greed Index is a 0-to-100 gauge that measures investor appetite, where 0 is extreme fear and 100 extreme greed. The index peaked at 82 on Aug. 26, its high for the year, and read 68 a month ago.
Bitcoin peaked at $86,978 early last week and slid as low as $81,749.83 on Oct. 8, a drop of about 6%, before recovering to roughly $83,800 on Monday. That leaves the largest cryptocurrency about 34% below its all-time high of above $126,000, set on Oct. 6, 2025 back when extreme greed was the norm.
That slide marked a rough stretch that extended until August of this year. The August rally led to a 24.9% increase in the price of Bitcoin, enough for industry participants such as Fundstrat co-founder and Bitmine Chairman Tom Lee and Crypto Quant’s Kim Yong Yu to announce the end of the bear market.
But the increased appetite for crypto bets has now cooled, at least for now, as the Fear and Greed Index indicates.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $484.9 million last week on Wednesday, their worst day since June, and another $244.1 million the following day. A $21.1 million inflow on Friday left the funds down a net $386.3 million for October while Ethereum funds extended their outflow streak to nine days, with $635 million out this month.
In terms of catalysts, macroeconomic headwinds have weighed on Bitcoin and the rest of crypto.
Brent crude topped $101 a barrel last week as ship attacks around the Strait of Hormuz piled up, and the 30-year Treasury yield hit 5.70%, its highest since 2002. Stocks, gold and Bitcoin sold off together that day, which points to a macro trade rather than a crypto problem. Brent is trading near $110 today, even after President Donald Trump said the U.S. would not engage in war at least until November.
Oil is an input cost for shipping, manufacturing, farming and travel, so a sustained jump in crude tends to filter into consumer prices. Higher inflation makes it harder for the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates and more likely to raise them, which is the path the central bank's latest minutes describe.
Bond investors respond by demanding higher yields, since inflation erodes the fixed payments Treasuries make. Because the Treasury yield is the benchmark "risk-free" return, a 30-year paying 5.70% pulls money away from riskier bets and raises borrowing costs across the economy. Bitcoin pays no yield and trades alongside stocks as a risk asset, so rising yields and rate-hike expectations tend to push it lower, as they did on Oct. 7.
The background likely explains why the Fear and Greed Index has dropped so much. Traders are more cautious, especially with high risk assets such as Bitcoin.
Traders on Myriad, a prediction market developed by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, give Bitcoin a 45% chance of touching $87,500 in October. That is down from 55% on Oct. 7. The odds of Bitcoin reaching $90,000 have slipped to 28% from 36%.
Myriad traders are also now pricing in 56% odds that Bitcoin drops to as low as $80,000, followed by 33% odds for a drop to $77,500 and 20% odds on $75,000.

items.title: Ledger Says All Confirmed Cases in Suspected $87M Drain Tied to Reseller CryptoBilis
items.content:
In brief
- Ledger said every confirmed case in last week's wallet-draining incident involves devices sold by Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis.
- The company said the number of affected devices is "limited," that it is working with authorities, and that CryptoBilis has ceased all hardware wallet sales.
- Ledger told authorized resellers never to restock returned products, and urged buyers to avoid unauthorized sellers.
Ledger said all confirmed cases in last week's draining incident involve devices sold through reseller CryptoBilis, and that its own systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected, in a 72-hour update on Sunday.
"The volume of impacted devices is limited," the Paris-based hardware wallet manufacturer said, adding that it is working with relevant authorities and reaching out to affected users. It said CryptoBilis has confirmed it has ceased all sales of hardware wallets.
72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident 🔽
As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.…
— Ledger (@Ledger) October 11, 2026
Ledger began investigating on Friday after users in Southeast Asia who bought devices from CryptoBilis reported losing funds. Onchain investigator Specter traced more than $86 million in suspected thefts across Ethereum, Tron and Bitcoin. Ledger has not confirmed that figure or said what caused the losses.
Onchain investigators YFarmX said they had sent Ledger a list of more than 450 drained wallets. According to their analysis, the thief pushed 2,810 ETH through coin mixer Tornado Cash in three runs, moved the withdrawals through Zcash's shielded pool, and withdrew about 3.28 million USDC into three fresh wallets, which Circle could freeze.
The thief also converted 15 million of the stolen USDT into USDD, a stablecoin Tether cannot freeze, before swapping 5.1 million back into USDT and sending about 4.23 million USDT to Binance deposit addresses, YFarmX said. Tether froze 10 million USDT on the first day, while 15,475 ETH, 203 BTC and 10 million USDD remain out of reach, according to the firm. Its findings have not been independently verified.
An X user, Johannes, has claimed to have found tampered Ledger devices in Europe, after buying two devices from retail stores. He said both had "identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module)," and called on Ledger to issue a product recall.
The claims have not been independently verified, and Ledger's update said all confirmed cases so far involve CryptoBilis devices. He said he is sending the second device to Ledger for analysis. Decrypt has reached out to Ledger for comment on the European reports.
Reseller controls
In its update, Ledger said it is reminding authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and "never to restock returned products."
It also warned users against buying from unauthorized resellers, where "the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important."
The company said it is reviewing reseller controls and advancing hardware protections, and called on others in the industry to work with it on supply-chain and anti-tamper practices.
Ledger repeated its advice that CryptoBilis buyers should not set up unused devices, and that anyone who already has should move their funds to a new seed phrase on a device bought from Ledger.
It also warned that scammers may try to exploit the incident, saying it "will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase."

Bitcoin drops 2.2% as Ukraine, Iran strikes send oil toward one-month high
Bitcoin price action stayed rangebound after failing to sustain above $84,000 into the Wall Street open on rising oil prices.
Bitcoin (BTC) gave back early-week gains into Monday’s Wall Street open as doubts compounded over a Russia-Ukraine “energy ceasefire.”
Key points:
- Bitcoin reached $84,250 before falling 2.2% amid market nerves over oil supplies and the Russia-Ukraine “energy ceasefire.”
- Analysis saw too much “risk premium” priced in to oil markets in the face of improving shipping volumes.
- BTC options traders positioned “defensively” while keeping $90,000 and above on the table.
Bitcoin pressured as Brent crude oil rises above $107
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD reaching $84,254 on Bitstamp, its highest level since Wednesday, before dropping up to 2.2%.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The retreat came as Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of continuing to target energy infrastructure despite US president Donald Trump announcing a moratorium on such strikes. Elsewhere, Iran reported that an oil tanker had been hit and was ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz.
Oil prices reacted sharply, with WTI crude spiking past $94 per barrel and Brent crude reaching $107.25 — its highest since Sept. 16.
CFDs on Brent crude oil four-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
The increases come with markets already on edge ahead of key US inflation data in the form of Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI), due out on Wednesday and Thursday respectively. As Cointelegraph reported, CPI has proven particularly sensitive to rising oil prices.
Commenting, Robin Brooks, former chief FX strategist at Goldman Sachs, argued that oil markets had priced in “too much risk premium,” pointing to improving Hormuz transit volumes.
“Oil volumes out of the Persian Gulf are around 13 mb/d compared to a high of 16.5 mb/d a few weeks ago. This is still way better than the height of the war in March and April, but oil prices are back to their highs,” he noted in a blog post on the day.
BTC bid support seeks to protect $82,000 
Looking ahead to possible BTC price targets, trading company QCP Capital reported duality in Bitcoin options markets, with “defensive” positioning combined with traders considering an upside breakout to still be possible.
Related: BTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week
“Implied volatility has held firm even as spot settled back into the range, while risk reversals show a less pronounced premium for puts than usual. Read together, the market looks less defensively positioned but still priced for a possible breakout,” it summarized in its latest analysis.
“A clean move above $87k would bring $94k into focus.”
Trader and analyst Rekt Capital flagged $83,400 as local resistance on the day, with that level mirroring the area around $77,000 from mid-August through Sept. 21, when BTC/USD broke higher.
BTC/USD one-day chart. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
Data from CoinGlass showed ask liquidity clustered around $84,500 on exchanges, with the total at that level circling $180 million. Bids were building around $82,000 at the time of writing, with spot price trending toward that level.

items.title: Eclair merges fixes for Lightning flaws that could burn Bitcoin in fees
items.content:
Quick Take
- Eclair merged October repairs that limit peer-selected replacement fees when nodes contribute funds to channel openings or splices.
- In Eclair-signer mode, new checks verify actual fees against supplied budgets and confirm rebuilt contributions pay the same fee.
- September's v0.14.3 remains the latest listed release, so the October merges alone do not confirm a packaged upgrade.
Eclair, ACINQ's Lightning node software, has merged two repairs for gaps that could make a node lose Bitcoin through excessive mining fees during channel funding and splicing. One limits a peer's fee-bump demands when Eclair contributes funds; the other checks transactions from a compromised Bitcoin backend while Eclair retains the signing keys.
The repairs merged into the project's master branch on Oct. 2 and Oct. 5. As of Oct. 12, its release page still listed September's v0.14.3 as latest. The two October fixes postdate that packaged release.
Bitcoin Optech's Oct. 9 newsletter highlighted both changes as closing protection gaps during dual funding and splicing.
The first repair, PR #3388, concerns peer-initiated replace-by-fee, or RBF, attempts during a dual-funded channel opening or a splice that adjusts a channel's funding. A peer could request a replacement transaction with a higher fee rate. Eclair kept its wallet contribution and paid for its inputs at that rate, without an upper bound or fee budget on this path.
That let a malicious peer impose an arbitrary mining fee rate on the contributing node while contributing nothing itself. The loss would be paid as fees to miners rather than transferred directly to the peer.
The repair rejects attempts above the maximum funding fee rate Eclair recommends to its peer. Two exceptions remain: the peer buys liquidity and pays the fees for Eclair's inputs, or the Eclair node contributes no funds to the transaction. In those cases, Eclair does not bear the cost addressed by this limit.
Keeping keys is only part of the defense
PR #3390 addresses a separate threat in Eclair-signer mode. Bitcoin Core's backend, bitcoind, selects coins and builds transactions, while Eclair retains the keys and signs.
A compromised backend could report a fee within budget while constructing a transaction that actually paid more, including by dropping the change output. Under Bitcoin's transaction accounting, input value not assigned to outputs becomes a miner fee. Missing change can therefore spend funds without paying an attacker's address.
When a fee budget is supplied, the repair calculates the actual fee from the amounts of the coins being spent, fetched by transaction ID to authenticate their values. It checks that the backend's reported fee matches and applies the budget to the actual fee. It also checks that Eclair's rebuilt contributions pay the same verified fee and rejects invalid change-output positions.
These are distinct from the cooperative-closing fee flaw covered in CryptoSlate's September report and the restart denial-of-service issues covered Oct. 2.
These repairs address Eclair's dual-funding, splicing and signer configurations. Operators should check that their installed build contains the October changes.

items.title: Palantir's Europe head warns the region is 'missing the boat' on AI just as it did with the internet
items.content:
Palantir's Europe head warns the region is 'missing the boat' on AI just as it did with the internet
The Palantir UK chief said the U.S. is racing ahead on enterprise AI while Europe hesitates, and explained why he thinks the company faces intense political attacks.
- Palantir’s head of U.K. and Europe Louis Mosley warned that Europe’s cautious approach to artificial intelligence risks repeating its failure to capitalize on the internet economy.
- Mosley described Palantir as a proxy for AI adoption, citing strong growth in its U.S. commercial revenue while European companies remain hesitant.
- Palantir faces European opposition over its defense and law enforcement contracts, but Mosley argued that political controversy distracts from AI’s potential to improve public services and productivity.
Palantir (PLTR) head of U.K. and Europe Louis Mosley warned that the region is making the same mistake with artificial intelligence (AI) that it made with the internet.
Where the U.S. "got the internet right," built a score of businesses and became the backbone of the digital economy, Europe "missed the boat," Mosley told CoinDesk in an interview.
The divergence between the markets in the decades since has been stark. Europe and the U.S. were roughly comparable 20 years ago on GDP per capita, capital-market depth and the scale of their largest companies. Since then, the U.S. has compounded growth while Europe has barely advanced in comparison.
Previous technology waves produced European champions. The internet wave produced almost none, with ASML (ASML) the rare exception, he said.
“It’s by far and away the largest European company. Which is, it tells you that the value is in tech,” he said.
Mosley, Palantir's executive vice president for the U.K and Europe, argued AI will be even more consequential. European corporates remain cautious, with an attitude of “This is new, that means it could be risky. I’ll wait and see,” according to Mosley.
Palantir builds an ontology and governance scaffold that lets governments and companies deploy large language models and agents in healthcare, industry or defense.
Mosley called the company “the purest proxy on public markets for the rate of AI adoption in an economy.” Palantir is model-agnostic: customers can run OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Grok, open-weight models or Chinese systems and fine-tune them on their own data.
Opposition to Palantir across the U.K. and Europe stems from its deep defense and law enforcement ties, including providing surveillance software to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) under the administration of President Donald Trump and supplying targeting systems to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). Campaigners have argued against the use of Palantir in systems used by the public services such as the U.K.'s National Health Service (NHS) on ethical grounds.
“The issues that really get those people fired up are Gaza and Trump," Mosley told CoinDesk. "Palantir has contracts in America for Trump’s administration and has contracts in Israel with the IDF and we have a contract with the NHS.”
Mosley called this a distraction from domestic priorities, asking whether politicians would tell a constituent they must wait longer for a hip operation because of a supplier’s unrelated foreign contracts.
Political hostility to energy-intensive tech is commonplace: bitcoin miners were attacked over electricity use a decade ago. Many of them have now pivoted to AI high-performance computing and face identical criticism over power consumption.
While it’s true AI will disrupt jobs, it will also free nurses and police from paperwork, raising productivity, he said. With only around 1,000 customers against a far larger addressable market of complex organizations in allied countries, Mosley said he still sees Palantir as early.
The biggest risk to AI, he said, remains political failure to explain why the technology is good for people.
“You’re making all the same mistakes again,” Mosley noted of the recurring political response. “In the end, I want to believe that good wins out over bad.”

items.title: NEXTPredict Paid $12,000 to Hedge Its Conference on a Prediction Market
items.content:
In brief
- NEXTPredict bought contracts on Kalshi that pay out if more than half of flights into JFK are canceled on October 21.
- The premium was $12,000 against roughly $3 million of coverage, the organizer's full investment in the event.
- Susquehanna took the other side as market maker, in what the parties call the first conference hedged on a prediction market.
The organizers of a prediction markets conference have hedged the conference on a prediction market, paying a $12,000 premium for contracts that would return around $3 million if New York's airports seize up the day before it opens.
The trade, executed through Kalshi with Susquehanna as market maker, settles on whether more than half of flights scheduled to land at John F. Kennedy International Airport are canceled on October 21, the main travel day before NEXTPredict's October 22-23 summit at Convene in Hudson Yards. The $3 million represents the organizer's total investment in the event.
This is me announcing a conference that never happened.
Today we hedged our next one on a prediction market. $3 million in coverage for a $12,000 premium, executed through @Kalshi with @SusquehannaSIG as market maker.
First time anyone in our event industry has done it. Here… pic.twitter.com/UtiA1xTXJw
— Pierre Lindh (@Pierreobv) July 28, 2026
The threshold was chosen as a proxy, Pierre Lindh, co-founder and managing director of NEXT.io, told Decrypt. “We had a conversation with Kalshi and Susquehanna, and we said, ‘Why don’t we use airport disruption as the vector?’ Because if there is 50% flight cancellation from JFK on the 21st of October, it means that something has happened in the world."
The risk is all too real. Lindh opened a thread on the trade with an image of himself announcing a conference in 2020 that never took place. "A few months later the entire world locked down and we lost 100% of our revenue for the entire year," he wrote.
Across 13 years and around 800 events the exposure has recurred. A blizzard hit New York weeks before the company's March show there, and conflict in the Middle East escalated shortly before it opened, leaving delegates unable to travel and the company processing refunds, he said. By May, with its flagship Malta event approaching, the worry was European airports running short of fuel.
"Event insurance is focused around what happens inside the venue," Lindh told Decrypt, describing cover for fires, rigging failures and injuries. Standard force majeure cover typically only pays out when an event is canceled. If a hurricane closes the airport, he said, "it doesn't mean that we have to cancel our conference. It probably means that we will need to organize it but short-handed." The costs are already sunk and the revenue is already lost, but the policy may never trigger, he told trade publication G3 Newswire. "The material financial damage has already happened, but standard event insurance might not trigger because the conference itself went ahead."
Force majeure has historically "just been accepted as part of the deal," he said. "You commit millions, you cross your fingers."
Lindh's second objection is the claim itself: insurance is slow to arrange and, he says, "when the moment comes, the insurer's incentive is to find the reason not to pay."
A market settles differently. Claiming on a policy means a potential argument with the insurer over whether the circumstances qualify, Lindh told the trade publication G3 Newswire, whereas on a prediction market, "Kalshi is in the middle determining whether the conditions of the contract have been met."
Kalshi self-certified the flight cancellation contracts with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on July 14 and built this market to order after NEXT.io approached it as an institutional customer. Retail traders cannot access it. Certain causes of disruption, including drone incidents and bomb threats, do not trigger payment.
The contracts drew criticism when they appeared, on the grounds that someone could profit by disrupting flights. Lindh addressed it directly, calling the worry fair and arguing that the hedge is the other face of the same instrument: "A business with real exposure, buying protection, on a regulated venue, with an institutional market maker taking the other side."
Both counterparties see a larger market behind it. Kalshi chief executive Tarek Mansour called it "prediction markets moving beyond forecasting and becoming practical business infrastructure." Joe Grubb, who heads prediction markets business development at Susquehanna, said the structure allows the transfer of institutional risk "that historically had no path for execution."
Lindh expects company. "Our whole industry has been carrying this risk on the chin for decades because there was no instrument for it," he wrote. "Now there is one."

items.title: XRP Ledger’s Payment Engine Had a Counterfeiting Bug Hiding Since 2015
items.content:
In brief
- XRP Ledger maintainers disclosed and patched a critical payment-engine overflow bug, reported via bug bounty in September, that could have let an attacker create counterfeit XRP.
- The flaw sat unnoticed since 2015 because no normal payment triggers it, and the ledger’s “no XRP created” safety check used the same broken arithmetic.
- There is no evidence the bug was ever exploited, XRP Ledger devs say.
Developers behind the XRP Ledger have disclosed and fixed a critical vulnerability that, left unaddressed, could have let an attacker conjure XRP out of thin air, a flaw that sat dormant in the network’s code for roughly a decade.
In a disclosure published Friday, the ledger’s maintainers said a researcher reported the bug through the XRPL bug bounty program in September. The issue was an integer overflow in the payment engine, the part of the software that processes payments.
When a single payment consumed hundreds of specially crafted offers from the order book, the sum of what the buyer owed exceeded the maximum value the system could store and “wrapped around” to a tiny number. The engine paid each seller in full but charged the buyer almost nothing, with the difference amounting to newly minted XRP that should never have existed.
Worse, the ledger’s built-in safety check meant to confirm no transaction creates XRP used the same flawed arithmetic, so it wrapped around identically and caught nothing. The maintainers said an attacker could have created spendable XRP far beyond the token’s total supply in a single transaction, then moved it, traded it or sent it to exchanges.
RippleX engineers confirmed the bug had been present since the current payment engine was written in 2015 and went unnoticed because no ordinary payment comes anywhere near triggering the overflow.
There is no evidence it was ever exploited, the team said. The fix shipped in version 3.4.1 on Sept. 25, and more than 80% of the network’s trusted validators were running it that day.
Notably, the patch bypassed the ledger’s usual amendment process, which requires validators to vote and wait two weeks before a change takes effect, the first time a transaction-processing change has deliberately shipped that way since the system was introduced over a decade ago. The maintainers said the severity justified it, since the open-source fix would have revealed the bug while leaving it exploitable for weeks.
The disclosure echoes a counterfeiting scare that rocked Zcash this year, when the privacy coin raced to patch a soundness bug in its shielded pool that could have allowed forged coins. That episode sent ZEC tumbling before the network’s Ironwood upgrade resolved it.
XRP didn’t escape the week unscathed. The token traded at $1.38 on Monday, down 1.6% over 24 hours, the worst performance among major cryptocurrencies, and off 9.4% over the past seven days.

items.title: Tom Lee sees $2 trillion wealth transfer fueling crypto demand as Bitmine buys more ether
items.content:
Tom Lee sees $2 trillion wealth transfer fueling crypto demand as Bitmine buys more ether
The Bitmine chairman said he expects younger investors to drive demand for digital assets as his ether treasury company inches closer to owning 5% of the total supply.
- Wall Street veteran Tom Lee sees a wealth transfer of up to $2 trillion between 2026 and 2028 as a potential driver of digital asset demand.
- Bitmine bought another 12,532 ETH last week, worth about $32 million at current prices, leaving it only weeks from achieving its goal of owning 5% of ether’s supply.
- Lee said Bitmine will stop buying ETH after reaching that target.
Tom Lee, chairman of ether 
Lee, a Wall Street veteran who also co-founded financial research and asset management firm Fundstrat in 2014 and serves as its chief investment officer, pointed to estimates from the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and Fundstrat suggesting between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion in wealth could change hands from 2026 through 2028.
"The wealth transfer underway is expected to support the upcoming crypto bull market as those inheriting wealth are younger and likely have a higher risk appetite for crypto and equities," Lee said in a Monday statement.
His remarks echoed what Vlad Tenev, CEO of digital brokerage Robinhood, highlighted in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer last month, saying more than $100 trillion in wealth is set to pass from older to younger generations over the coming decades.
The idea is that younger investors may put more of their inherited money into crypto than previous generations, adding another source of demand. How much of that wealth will actually reach digital assets, though, is unclear.
Lee also noted Wall Street's growing use of blockchain technology to represent financial assets, the rise of AI applications and crypto treasury companies holding tokens for the long term as possible drivers of a new rally.
Bitmine inches closer to its 5% ETH goal
Lee's remarks came alongside Bitmine's latest crypto holdings update, which showed the ether treasury firm inching closer to its goal of owning 5% of the token's supply.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies 
The purchase lifted its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, worth roughly $15.3 billion. That's about 4.9% of ether’s 122.1 million token supply, leaving the company some 76,000 ETH short of its goal of owning 5%.
At last week's pace, Bitmine could hit that target in about six weeks.
Lee said last week the company plans to stop accumulating ETH once it reaches the 5% mark. Since its pivot to an ether-focused strategy in June 2025, the firm said it bought ETH every week.
Bitmine has staked about 5.07 million ETH, or 84% of its holdings, and projects roughly $336 million in annualized staking revenue at current yields.

items.title: France’s tax proposal would tax Bitcoin-to-USDC swaps before investors cash out
items.content:
Quick Take
- France’s committee-approved amendment would recognize gains or losses on swaps into MiCA e-money tokens, before any cash withdrawal.
- Pre-2027 holdings would have two basis routes; the irrevocable allocation option could shift how much gain the first disposal recognizes.
- Taxable swaps would reset received tokens’ basis, while existing rules would still prevent net crypto losses offsetting later-year gains.
France’s proposed crypto tax changes would make a move from Bitcoin or Ether into certain stablecoins a taxable disposal, even if the investor never withdraws cash.
The National Assembly’s Finance Committee adopted amendment I-CF1826 on Oct. 7, adding that proposed exception to a broader overhaul of how private crypto gains are calculated. The provision would apply to disposals and exchanges from Jan. 1, 2027 if enacted.
For an investor selling Bitcoin exposure into USDC, the consequence would be a change in the tax timing of a risk-reduction trade. A gain could become reportable while the proceeds remain in a crypto wallet or exchange account. But the proposal also changes the cost deducted from those proceeds, and gives older holdings a transition choice.
Under French tax authority guidance, covered crypto-to-crypto exchanges without a cash balancing payment receive tax deferral. Converting into fiat or using crypto to obtain other goods or services can already be taxable under the private-disposal regime, subject to its applicable exemption.
CF1826 would remove the exchange deferral when the investor receives e-money tokens as defined by the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, or related rights. The operative wording targets the asset received. A swap out of Bitcoin into a qualifying token could therefore recognize a gain before any later cash withdrawal.
MiCA’s definition describes a crypto-asset that seeks to maintain stable value by reference to one official currency. That legal definition sets the exception’s scope. The amendment invokes it without an express issuer-licensing condition.
USDC provides a concrete example: Circle’s European white paper identifies it as an e-money token under the same MiCA provision. The illustrations below use native USDC, with transactions measured in euros.
The amendment’s sponsors justify the change by describing deferral on fiat-backed stablecoin conversions as a legislative loophole. For an investor using a swap to reduce market exposure, the practical effect would be earlier recognition of any gain.
The proposed tax calculation concerns the gain above cost. It subtracts the acquisition basis of the assets surrendered from the disposal price. That basis is the cost recognized for tax purposes; a transaction can produce a gain, no gain or a loss.
Two ways to value older holdings
France’s existing portfolio-based calculation allocates part of the acquisition price of the entire crypto portfolio to each taxable disposal. Current guidance deducts total portfolio acquisition price multiplied by the ratio of disposal price to portfolio value immediately before the transaction.
The proposed replacement would focus on the crypto-assets actually disposed of. For assets of the same nature purchased at different prices, it specifies weighted-average acquisition value.
For holdings acquired before 2027, the amendment offers two routes. An investor could use evidenced actual acquisition costs, determined under the new basis rules. Alternatively, the investor could allocate the portfolio acquisition price calculated under the old rules at Dec. 31, 2026 among the assets held then, in proportion to their values on that date.
The allocation option preserves a pool of acquisition cost and distributes it among holdings. The available cost pool remains the acquisition price calculated under the old rules, rather than the portfolio’s full market value. The text makes that choice irrevocable for the entire portfolio when the first return reporting a taxable disposal after Jan. 1, 2027 is filed.
Consider a hypothetical investor whose Bitcoin cost €20,000 and is worth €60,000, while their Ether cost €40,000 and is worth €40,000 at the transition date. The portfolio has €60,000 of acquisition cost and a €100,000 value. Assume no prior disposals, fees or cash balancing payments, no other holdings of the same tokens, and unchanged euro values through the transactions.
Under the allocation option, Bitcoin represents 60% of the portfolio value and receives €36,000 of basis. Ether receives the remaining €24,000. Using actual costs instead would leave their bases at €20,000 and €40,000, respectively.
The same Bitcoin-to-USDC transaction would then produce different first-disposal gains:
| Hypothetical transaction or basis | Proposed actual-cost route | Proposed allocation route | 
|---|---|---|
| Bitcoin basis before the swap | €20,000 | €36,000 | 
| Gain on swap into €60,000 of native USDC | €40,000 | €24,000 | 
| Basis of the USDC received | €60,000 | €60,000 | 
| Gain on later Ether disposal for €40,000 | €0 | €16,000 | 
The table compares hypothetical gross gains under the proposal. Under the current rules, the qualifying swap itself would receive deferral. Under either proposed transition route, the Bitcoin-to-USDC swap would become a taxable event.
Changing only the historical costs to €50,000 for Bitcoin and €10,000 for Ether reverses the first-disposal comparison: actual cost would produce a €10,000 Bitcoin gain against allocation’s €24,000. The remaining Ether gain at unchanged values would be €30,000 under actual cost or €16,000 under allocation. Historical costs determine which method recognizes more gain first.
Basis resets and the cost of loss timing
The proposal expressly distinguishes exchanges that retain deferral from exchanges that become taxable. A deferred exchange carries the surrendered assets’ basis into the assets received. A taxable exchange gives the received crypto-assets a basis based on the consideration value already used to calculate the gain, adjusted for any cash balancing payment.
For the Bitcoin-to-USDC swap in the first example, the reset rule would give the USDC received €60,000 of basis under either transition route. Selling it later for the same €60,000 would produce no further gain. That reset would prevent repeat recognition of the original Bitcoin gain when the unchanged-value proceeds finally reached a bank account.
USDC references the dollar, so the unchanged-euro-value assumption is essential. A later disposal at a different euro value would require its own gain or loss calculation.
If the investor also sold the remaining Ether for €40,000, the first example would produce aggregate realized gains of €40,000 under either proposed transition route. Actual cost recognizes all of that in Bitcoin; allocation splits it between Bitcoin and Ether.
The amendment would change the swap exception and basis rules without rewriting the existing crypto loss restriction. The tax authority says crypto gains and losses offset within the same tax year, while a net crypto loss cannot be carried into later years or used against gains on other assets.
A separate hypothetical shows the effect of recognizing losses and gains in different years. Under the proposed actual-basis rules, a sole Bitcoin holding bought for €30,000 and swapped into €20,000 of native USDC would recognize a €10,000 loss. The USDC would receive €20,000 of basis.
If that USDC were later exchanged into Bitcoin without a cash balancing payment, the swap would retain deferral because Bitcoin is outside the received e-money-token exception. It would carry the €20,000 basis into Bitcoin. A subsequent taxable Bitcoin sale for €30,000 would recognize a €10,000 gain. Assume no fees, other token pools, cash adjustments or other gains and losses.
Those amounts could offset if realized in the same tax year. If the net loss arose in one year and the gain in a later year, the earlier loss would not shelter that later gain under the existing rule. Recognition in different years can therefore change the taxable result even when the transaction sequence returns the holding to its original value.
The reporting trade-off follows from the same mechanics. Asset-specific basis would remove the portfolio-wide allocation formula for new disposals, but investors would need to preserve acquisition evidence, weighted averages and the basis carried or reset through swaps. For older holdings, the proposed allocation route would also require a Dec. 31 valuation and a whole-portfolio decision that the text makes irrevocable.
The next legislative test remains ahead. The 2027 budget dossier, checked Oct. 12, lists National Assembly plenary discussion for Oct. 13.

It is also probably the prediction that sentiment has changed on the most in the direction away from Kelly, since 2016. After a decade of evidence and updating, f...

Aside: I think the biggest interesting prediction he had was that AI would obey a user driven network effect. It seems like a very clean prediction, and yet it has failed to m...

[cousinbryce]: Google’s main product was and continues to be ads

Stockfish still beats the newest, largest LLM at chess.  Etc.  Most of the truly productive "AI" is customized for a specific purpose, or class of purposes anyway.

items.title: 两年超30亿美元！Stripe、万事达卡、Circle接连收购稳定币公司
items.content:
两年超30亿美元！Stripe、万事达卡、Circle接连收购稳定币公司

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，风险投资人 Alex Lazarow 撰文称，过去两年，Stripe、万事达卡和 Circle 分别收购美国稳定币基础设施公司 Bridge、英国 BVNK 及新加坡跨境支付平台 Tazapay，三笔交易总价值超过 30 亿美元。这三家公司成立于 2020 年至 2022 年间，累计融资约 2 亿美元，显示稳定币支付基础设施正成为传统支付巨头及加密企业争相布局的领域。

其中，Stripe 于 2024 年宣布以略高于 10 亿美元的价格收购 Bridge；万事达卡收购 BVNK 的交易总价值最高达 18 亿美元，包括 15 亿美元基础对价及 3 亿美元或有对价；Circle 则同意以 4 亿美元股票收购 Tazapay，交易预计于 2027 年完成。

稳定币采用率增长、监管框架逐步明晰及跨境实时支付需求上升，是推动并购的主要因素。数据显示，2025 年稳定币调整后交易量同比增长 91%，达到 10.9 万亿美元，接近 Visa 的 14.2 万亿美元；现实世界支付规模则增长逾一倍，达到约 3900 亿美元。

这些交易反映出收购方看重的不只是稳定币技术，还包括已验证的业务规模、支付网络及合规资质。随着稳定币支付基础设施成熟，美元账户、稳定币支付卡和跨境汇款等应用也在兴起，未来全球各地区可能出现更多类似 Bridge 和 BVNK 的本地基础设施公司被收购。

items.title: Tokenized catastrophe bonds target the disaster-insurance gap
items.content:
Tokenized catastrophe bonds target the disaster-insurance gap
A planned Bermuda issuance would put legal ownership onchain and seek capital for disaster risks that remain costly to insure.
- Natural disasters caused $220 billion in economic losses last year, but insurance covered only $107 billion, leaving households, businesses and governments to bear the rest.
- The catastrophe-bond market reached $65.6 billion in June, as insurers increasingly transferred disaster risks to investors despite persistent coverage gaps, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region.
- Harneys and dropRWA plan to issue tokenized catastrophe bonds in early 2027, potentially widening investor access through smaller ownership units while remaining subject to securities, insurance and investor-protection rules.
Natural disasters caused $220 billion in economic losses last year. Insurance covered only $107 billion of that bill, according to Swiss Re, leaving households, businesses and governments to absorb the rest.
Capital has continued to flow into catastrophe bonds. Catastrophe bonds, or cat bonds, let insurers pass the financial risk of a hurricane, wildfire or earthquake to capital-market investors. The market had $65.6 billion outstanding in June and new issuance reached $11.3 billion in the second quarter, the largest quarterly total on record, according to Artemis’ recent cat bond report.
Yet large parts of the loss from floods, typhoons and wildfires remain uninsured. In the Asia-Pacific, 91% of disaster losses in 2023 were uninsured, according to the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). It also said limited claims data and catastrophe models can make it harder for insurers and reinsurers to price coverage, particularly in high-risk areas.
Harneys, a Bermuda-based law firm specializing in global insurance, and tokenization platform dropRWA plan to issue tokenized cat bonds early next year, with each token representing legal ownership of the catastrophe bond.
The proposal builds on a conventional market that has historically been available largely to specialist funds and large institutions. Many catastrophe-bond offerings carry minimum investments of $250,000 or more. Harneys and droppRWA are considering a structure that could accommodate smaller beneficial interests, though it would still need to comply with securities, insurance and investor-protection rules.
Henry Tucker, chief executive of specialist insurance group Hearns, said a tokenized structure does not turn disaster coverage into a casual retail investment. The capital is fully committed to cover a defined insurance risk. “You’re not buying a right to get paid by somebody else who’s bet the other way at the casino,” he told CoinDesk in an interview.
Tucker pointed to flood cover and typhoon protection in Southeast Asia as risks that can be difficult to place with conventional reinsurers, particularly when claims data is limited or loss estimates are uncertain. A specialist underwriter could use a tokenized structure to raise capital for a single defined risk and set out the assumptions and the return offered to investors.
There is a real-world precedent for using catastrophe bonds to finance public disaster protection. The World Bank arranged $200 million of hurricane coverage for Jamaica in May, replacing an earlier transaction that paid out after Hurricane Melissa in 2025. Jamaica’s finance minister, Fayval Williams, called catastrophe bonds “an important piece ensuring capital market access” for the country’s resilience strategy.
Tokenization will not make a hurricane, flood or wildfire less expensive, Tucker said. Nor will it guarantee cheaper insurance for people in exposed areas, he added. The firms’ argument is that a token serving as the legal ownership record, combined with smaller ownership units, could bring more investors into a market built to absorb extreme losses.

items.title: 大摩称市场过度担忧AI数据中心800V供电延期，OCP峰会或成半导体股催化剂
items.content:
大摩称市场过度担忧AI数据中心800V供电延期，OCP峰会或成半导体股催化剂

动察 Beating AI 快讯，摩根士丹利今日发布研报称，市场对 AI 数据中心原生 800V 直流供电技术部署延期的担忧可能已经过度。英伟达下一代 AI 服务器机柜全面采用原生 800V 供电的时间或推迟至 2028 年前后，但整体技术转型方向并未改变，10 月 12 日至 15 日举行的开放计算项目（OCP）全球峰会有望成为相关半导体股票的积极催化剂。

大摩指出，英伟达原计划在 2027 年下半年推出的 Rubin Ultra 系列中引入原生 800V 供电，但相关机柜方案正在调整。英伟达最新路线图显示，第三代、功率约 570 千瓦的服务器机柜仍采用 54V 直流配电，原生 800V 机柜可能要等到后续 Feynman 架构、功率约 1 兆瓦的产品世代。不过，800V 外置供电模块仍按计划出货，预计于 2027 年推出的 Power Center 集中供电系统也在持续推进。

估值方面，800V 相关企业未来 12 个月 EV/Sales 倍数已从 6 月高点回落至约 6.5 倍，基本回到今年 3 月英伟达 GTC 大会前的水平。但同期相关企业未来 12 个月预期营收增速已从约 12% 升至 27%，自首次出现部署延期报道以来，营收预测反而累计上调约 11%。

大摩认为，若 OCP 峰会进一步确认 800V 技术路线及后续部署安排，电源管理、模拟半导体和功率半导体板块有望受益，并特别提及亚德诺半导体、德州仪器、安森美、Wolfspeed 及纳微半导体。此外，AI 数据中心需求增长还可能推动成熟制程产能在 2027 年趋紧。

items.title: 美联储加息预期冲击抵押贷款债券市场，银行需求或进一步减弱
items.content:
美联储加息预期冲击抵押贷款债券市场，银行需求或进一步减弱

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，过去三周，投资者以历史罕见的速度撤离美国抵押贷款债券基金，资金流出规模均跻身 2021 年初以来最严重的七次之列。随着利率飙升，投资者纷纷寻求规避市场波动风险。美国抵押贷款支持证券指数 9 月录得有记录以来第二差的月度表现。

此前，美国国债收益率在油价飙升、通胀担忧加剧以及市场预期美联储加息的推动下升至数十年来的高位，引发抵押贷款债券抛售。抵押贷款支持证券（MBS）对债券收益率的突然波动高度敏感，因为债券收益率是整个经济体系借贷成本的定价基准。当利率上升时，房主通常会停止对住房贷款进行再融资，导致投资者持有低收益证券的时间超过此前预期。

策略师 Erica Adelberg 写道：「美联储收紧货币政策以及收益率曲线趋于平坦，可能削弱银行这一 MBS 重要买家的需求。积极的一面是，随着抵押贷款利率升至 2023 年以来最高水平，抑制再融资和购房需求，并可能减缓房价及贷款规模的增长，预计 MBS 供应量将在年底前呈下降趋势。」(金十)

items.title: Bitcoin’s rebound approaches the $85,000 zone where past buyers may sell
items.content:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin climbed above $84,000 while Ethereum reclaimed $2,500 as both cryptocurrencies extended their weekend recovery.
- Bitcoin approaches a dense $84,000–$85,000 acquisition-cost zone; Ethereum still had 10.58 million ETH of futures open interest in an Oct. 10 snapshot.
- A failed Bitcoin breakout could expose $77,000–$79,000 support, while renewed ETH volatility risks triggering fresh liquidations.
Bitcoin and Ethereum extended their weekend recovery, although on-chain indicators and derivatives positioning suggest the rebound faces significant obstacles.
Data from CryptoSlate showed that Bitcoin briefly climbed above $84,000 after falling toward $80,000 during last week's selloff. Ethereum also recovered above $2,500, reversing part of its recent losses as buying activity returned to the cryptocurrency market.
However, Bitcoin's advance has brought it closer to a major concentration of investor acquisition costs between $84,000 and $85,000, where selling pressure could intensify. Meanwhile, Ethereum's recovery comes as larger derivatives traders appear to be reducing their bullish exposure despite substantial outstanding positions.
Bitcoin's $85,000 resistance threatens to stall recovery
Bitcoin's recovery gained momentum during Sunday's trading session as traders appeared to capitalize on a liquidity concentration above the prevailing market price.
CryptoQuant analyst J.A. Maartunn said on Oct. 11 that a liquidity cluster formed just above Bitcoin's trading level, giving traders an opportunity to push prices higher.
According to Maartunn, traders appeared to establish a substantial wall of buy orders beneath the market, providing support as Bitcoin advanced toward the overhead liquidity.
The spot Bid/Ask Ratio, which measures buying and selling liquidity within 1% of the prevailing price, rose to 0.3.
The increase indicated that visible buying interest had strengthened relative to selling orders. Such liquidity can also disappear if traders cancel their orders.
Checkonchain data highlighted by analyst Darkfost on Oct. 11 showed that approximately 53% of Bitcoin's invested capital had an estimated acquisition price above $83,000 when the cryptocurrency traded around that level.
The measure weights acquisition prices by invested capital, so larger positions carry more weight.
More importantly, the largest concentration of acquisition costs sits between $84,000 and $85,000, making the region a potential obstacle to further gains.
Investors who acquired Bitcoin around those levels could become more willing to sell as prices approach their estimated cost basis, increasing the supply that buyers must absorb.
A sustained move through the region would suggest buying demand is strong enough to overcome that potential selling pressure. If it fails to do so, Bitcoin could be vulnerable to another decline, with Darkfost identifying the $77,000 to $79,000 range as a possible support area.
Ethereum's $2,500 rebound faces risk from leveraged traders
Ethereum's recovery faces another challenge as derivatives positioning among larger market participants continues to deteriorate.
Alphractal CEO Joao Wedson noted on Oct. 10 that Ethereum's 30-day and 180-day open-interest deltas were both negative, along with weakening readings in its Whale vs. Retail Delta indicator.
He interpreted the combination as evidence that major traders have reduced their bullish exposure while increasingly favoring defensive or short positions.
The negative open-interest readings indicate that outstanding derivatives positions have contracted over the measured periods.
Despite the contraction, Ethereum's total futures open interest remained substantial at approximately 10.58 million ETH, indicating that considerable derivatives exposure was still outstanding.
Valued at $2,500 per ETH, that represents roughly $26.5 billion in notional exposure.
The combination of weakening bullish positioning and substantial remaining exposure increases the potential for sharp price movements if volatility returns.
A renewed decline could push leveraged long positions toward forced liquidation, potentially adding selling pressure and accelerating losses. Conversely, a sustained recovery could force short sellers to close positions, contributing to further upward momentum.
Wedson warned that Ethereum's derivatives market remains vulnerable to further liquidations despite the recent reduction in outstanding positions.
Bitcoin is -3.07% over the past 24 hours and currently sits at rank #1 by market cap.

Evernorth’s share price rose by 5% as investors welcomed the Nasdaq debut of the first pure-play XRP digital asset treasury.
The newly listed shares of XRP-focused treasury company Evernorth Holdings (XRPN) jumped as much as 5% on their Monday Nasdaq stock exchange debut, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Earlier on Monday, the company named former Coinbase Asset Management Co-Chief Investment Officer Hugo Jeandesboz as its new chief investment officer. He will lead treasury strategy, including treasury allocation, liquidity management and the active management of Evernorth’s XRP holdings, according to a Monday announcement.
Evernorth deploys its XRP holdings to earn additional income through decentralized finance (DeFi) yield strategies.
On Oct. 2, shareholders of blank-check firm Armada Acquisition Corp. II approved the plan to combine the company with Evernorth. The company expects to hold about 473 million XRP, currently worth $657 million, which it said would make it the largest publicly traded XRP treasury company.
As for the XRP token, it was recently trading hands at $1.39 apiece with $1.48 billion worth traded in the past 24 hours, according to Coingecko data. At that price, XRP has a market cap of roughly $87.8 billion, making it the fifth-biggest cryptocurrency.

items.title: Ledger implant tests Bitcoin ETFs as safer custodial solutions than hardware wallets
items.content:
Ledger implant tests Bitcoin ETFs as safer custodial solutions than hardware wallets
The discovery of an unauthorized Ledger hardware implant reignited debate on whether Bitcoin ETFs are safer than self-custodying Bitcoin via hardware wallet devices.
The newly discovered Ledger exploit has stirred broad industry debate over the safety of hardware wallets compared to effectively custodying Bitcoin holdings through exchange-traded funds (ETFs).
Bitcoin analyst Plan B said his then-controversial decision to move his Bitcoin (BTC) holdings to ETFs in 2025 was the right call in light of the recent Coldcard and Ledger exploits. “Zero regrets” about my ETF decision, wrote the analyst in a Monday X post.
Large holders have been converting self-custodied assets to ETFs for “enhanced security” for years, which is one of the main “selling points” for ETFs, 21Shares co-founder Ophelia Snyder told Cointelegraph in an email on Monday, adding that the recent exploits made this phenomenon part of the “public discourse.”
The remarks follow the discovery of a compromised Ledger wallet that contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Some blockchain investigators estimated that losses from these implants could top $86 million, raising questions about the security of self-custodial cold wallets.
Related: Standard Chartered plans institutional crypto custody in Singapore
Hardware wallets are still safe, but providers need better threat modelling: Adam Back
To be sure, hardware wallets can still be secure custodial options, but providers need a better understanding of the emerging threat landscape, according to Blockstream CEO and Hashcash inventor Adam Back.
“Surprisingly few manufacturers understood the generic attacks, or so it seemed from their marketing and design choices, for the last decade. Time to catch up with threat-modelling,” wrote Back in a Saturday X post.
Source: Adam Back
However, Snyder said the main issue with self-custodial wallets is that their security depends on investors’ technical expertise and individual setup. She said:
“Without taking the time and rigor to set up properly, self-custody will always be less secure than handing over the assets to a specialist firm whose job it is to manage those protocols for you.”
Bitcoin security researcher and cypherpunk Jameson Lopp also said that self-custodial wallets can be a robust option, but urged investors to avoid mass migration to create new central points of failure during rushed transactions.
Magazine: Bitcoiners turn to dice throws as self-custody setups are re-evaluated

items.title: 微软Agent负责人押注2027年AI不再等你提问，信息流直接送上工作成果
items.content:
微软Agent负责人押注2027年AI不再等你提问，信息流直接送上工作成果

动察 Beating AI 快讯，微软主动式 AI Agent 团队负责人 Nicolas Bustamante 预测，AI 信息流可能成为 2027 年的主流交互方式。

聊天模式把太多工作留给了用户：自己摸索 AI 能做什么、编写 Prompt、交代背景，还要反复指挥 Agent。要让数十亿人每天使用 Agent，就不能指望人人都学会这些操作。

他设想的 AI 信息流，更像一份自动更新的待办清单：需要回复的邮件，AI 已经写好草稿；销售数据刚更新，发给团队的报告也已准备好。用户像刷社交媒体一样浏览，批准、修改或忽略即可，遇到复杂问题再进入聊天。Meta 的 Muse 已经开始主动提出建议、执行任务。

这套模式还有一层商业逻辑。用户每天打开信息流，AI 就能根据个人计划推荐餐厅、商品或服务，通过明确标注的广告补贴 Agent 运行成本。

items.title: AMD推出Helion智能体AI机架方案，单机架最高支持32,768个CPU核心
items.content:
AMD推出Helion智能体AI机架方案，单机架最高支持32,768个CPU核心

动察 Beating AI 快讯，AMD 今日宣布推出 AMD Helion 智能体 AI 机架方案，采用基于开放计算项目（OCP）规范的开放式基础设施设计，旨在满足大规模 AI 智能体执行任务的算力需求，并支持 CPU 与 GPU 灵活组合。

AMD Helion 提供两种主要配置：一是搭载第六代 AMD EPYC 处理器的纯 CPU 机架，最高支持 32,768 个 CPU 核心，面向超大规模部署，为智能体执行任务提供专用算力，并连接独立的模型推理基础设施；二是整合 AMD EPYC CPU、AMD Instinct MI350P GPU 及通用计算节点的一体化机架，面向企业级智能体 AI 应用。

AMD 表示，Helion 支持液冷和风冷配置，客户可根据工作负载、性能、功耗及成本需求调整 CPU 与 GPU 资源。该方案还结合开放式软硬件及集成 Token 路由器，可将智能体的模型调用分配至前沿模型和开源模型。

AMD 计划将 Helion 规范提交至 OCP，供社区进一步开发和采用。目前，该方案正与生态合作伙伴共同开发，预计于 2026 年 11 月推出。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，高盛将未来三个月全球股票评级从「中性」上调至「增持」，并维持未来 12 个月的看多立场。高盛认为，企业盈利持续增长、股票估值从夏季高位回落，以及投资者持仓减少，改善了股票的风险回报比。

FactSet 数据显示，标普 500 指数未来 12 个月预期市盈率已从 6 月初的 21.1 倍降至 19.1 倍，年初约为 22 倍。高盛预计，标普 500 成分股第三季度盈利同比增长 27%，有望连续第三个季度实现超过 25% 的盈利增幅，AI 基础设施投资仍是重要驱动力。

区域配置方面，高盛维持对美国和亚洲股票的「增持」评级，对欧洲股票维持「减持」评级。同时，该行将未来 12 个月政府债券评级上调至「增持」，建议采用「杠铃策略」，一端配置科技股，另一端配置具有类似债券特征的股票，并偏好较短久期债券及现金资产。

items.title: Bitmine Adds $32M in Ethereum as Tom Lee Says Firm Is Nearly 'Done Stacking'
items.content:
In brief
- Bitmine acquired 12,532 ETH over the past week, bringing its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, or 4.9% of Ethereum's supply.
- Chairman Tom Lee said the firm needs about 100,000 more ETH to reach its 5% target, after which it will be "done stacking."
- Lee predicted the largest crypto bull market ever, citing tokenization, a generational wealth transfer and supply held by treasury firms.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies bought 12,532 ETH over the past week, worth about $31.9 million at the $2,544 price the company used to value its holdings and lifting its holdings to 6,028,946 ETH, the company said Monday.
The stash represents 4.9% of the total 122.1 million Ethereum token supply, leaving the firm 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5%, a target it calls the "Alchemy of 5%."
🧵
1/
BitMine provided its latest holdings update for October 12, 2026$16.2 billion in total crypto + "moonshots":
- 6,028,946 ETH at $2,544 per ETH (per @coinbase)
- 214 Bitcoin (BTC)
- $180 million stake in Beast Industries @MrBeast
- $85 million stake in Eightco Holdings…— Bitmine (NYSE-BMNR) $ETH $BMNP (@BitMNR) October 12, 2026
Bitmine bought $41 million more ETH the week before. In a press release, the firm's Chairman Tom Lee claimed that its “track record of consistent buying of crypto is unmatched by any public company in the world.”
The company valued its ETH at $2,544 per token, and put its total crypto, cash and investment holdings at $16.2 billion. That includes 214 BTC, $612 million in cash and marketable securities, and stakes worth $180 million in Beast Industries and $85 million in Eightco Holdings.
The firm has staked 5,067,309 ETH, which Lee said generates annualized staking revenue of about $336 million.
'Done stacking'
In his monthly Chairman's message last week, Lee said Bitmine needs "about 100,000 more ETH, and that's about it." He has said the firm's Ethereum buying will stop once it reaches its target.
"Now we're done stacking while a bull market is starting," Lee said in the video. "So if we're done stacking, but ETH goes up a lot, you can imagine that we'll outperform Ethereum."
Lee predicted the crypto bull market would be "the biggest bull market we've ever seen," driven by tokenization, a wealth transfer to younger investors, supply absorbed by digital asset treasury firms, and AI agents using crypto wallets.
He said Bitmine shares, then around $26, are 90% correlated with ETH, and projected that ETH at $22,000 would put the stock at $300 to $500.
Lee also pointed to Bitmine's 9.5% perpetual preferred stock, BMNP, which was issued at $80 in June and last closed at $99.53, according to the release.

分析：比特币本周或在81,300至84,500美元区间震荡，周三CPI将决定后续方向

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，Bitfinex Alpha 发布报告称，比特币本周走势将受到美国周三公布的 CPI 数据及现货买盘强度影响。报告预计，CPI 公布前，BTC 大概率在 81,300 至 84,500 美元区间震荡。

报告指出，BTC 从 10 月 2 日的 87,197 美元高点回落 7.9%，并于 10 月 8 日一度跌至 80,347 美元，随后重新收复 81,300 美元这一前期区间高点。同期，加密市场约 11.8 亿美元头寸遭清算，未平仓合约量此后尚未明显恢复，意味着下一轮行情更依赖现货市场需求。

items.title: 博通CEO警告：资本正取代芯片与电力，成为AI发展最大瓶颈
items.content:
博通CEO警告：资本正取代芯片与电力，成为AI发展最大瓶颈

动察 Beating AI 快讯，博通 CEO Hock Tan 在新加坡举行的 DBS Asia Future Forward 大会上表示，资本正取代芯片、存储和电力供应，成为 AI 行业发展的最大制约因素。他警告，许多 AI 投资者并不了解自己押注的技术，却期待获得高额回报，投资行为如同赌场下注。

Tan 以 OpenAI 为例指出，该公司 9 月年化收入已达 500 亿美元，但高昂的模型训练成本仍使其处于亏损状态，收入增长并不意味着商业模式已经得到验证。他还预计，晶圆短缺可能在 2028 至 2029 年间改善，电力供应也有望随着新基础设施投入使用而逐步宽松。

英特尔 CEO 陈立武也表示，融资成本上升和投资回报的不确定性正成为 AI 行业的核心挑战。尽管两人均认为未来两到三年算力需求仍将保持强劲，但 Tan 警告，如果先进 AI 模型的应用进展不及预期，或模型能力提升遭遇瓶颈，算力基础设施需求可能明显放缓。

items.title: EU targets MiCA loophole that lets crypto exchanges serve 27 countries with one license
items.content:
Quick Take
- EU finance ministers have agreed to place major crypto companies under direct ESMA supervision in a proposed overhaul of MiCA.
- The change aims to address regulatory gaps that allow crypto firms licensed in one country to serve customers across all 27 EU states.
- Only 10 to 15 of roughly 360 providers may face centralized oversight, leaving most firms under national regulators.
EU finance ministers agreed to shift oversight of major crypto companies to a central watchdog, reshaping supervision under MiCA.
The Council of the European Union reached a political agreement on Oct. 9 to give the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) direct responsibility for the bloc's most significant crypto-asset service providers, as part of a wider package to integrate European financial markets.
The proposed overhaul addresses a weakness in the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), which allows firms licensed in one member state to serve customers across the 27-country bloc while remaining primarily supervised by their home-country regulator.
The compromise, however, is considerably narrower than the European Commission's original plan to move all crypto service providers under ESMA. Officials estimate that only 10 to 15 of roughly 360 providers would qualify for centralized supervision, Reuters reported.
The agreement sets the Council's negotiating position rather than changing the law immediately. The Council must still negotiate the proposal with the European Parliament.
National licenses expose gap in EU-wide oversight
MiCA's passporting system was designed to provide crypto firms with a single route into the European market. Under the regulation, a provider authorized in one member state can offer approved services elsewhere in the EU without establishing a physical presence in every country it serves.
That arrangement reduces duplication for firms expanding across borders, but it also places considerable responsibility on the national authority issuing the initial approval. This is because a company's operations, client assets, and technology systems can grow well beyond the market where it was licensed.
The consequences emerged in a July 2025 ESMA review of the Malta Financial Services Authority's authorization of an unnamed crypto provider.
ESMA questioned why the company received approval while material issues remained unresolved. Its reviewers found insufficient evidence that the licensing assessment adequately addressed governance, potential conflicts of interest, technology infrastructure, custody arrangements and certain anti-money-laundering risks.
The review did not establish that every Maltese license was deficient. It also credited the Maltese regulator with sector expertise and sufficient supervisory resources, while recommending improvements to its authorization process.
Malta subsequently said it was implementing the recommendations but opposed transferring supervision to ESMA, arguing in September 2025 that MiCA was too new to justify an additional regulatory layer. The authority warned that centralization could introduce bureaucracy and hamper competitiveness.
The dispute highlighted a broader tension: one regulator's authorization decision can affect crypto customers across Europe, even when other national watchdogs view the required level of scrutiny differently.
Largest crypto providers face new thresholds and EU enforcement
In response, EU regulators are proposing a new framework to address these issues.
Under the Council's draft, ESMA would take direct oversight of crypto providers with at least 15 million active EU users, or those meeting three of five additional significance criteria covering their customer base, custody assets, transaction volumes and financial interconnectedness.
Those criteria include more than 1 million active users, over €1 billion in crypto assets under custody and more than €4 billion in annual client transactions.
Together, these factors mean a provider's overall scale and connections to the financial system, rather than its place of incorporation alone, would determine whether supervision moves to ESMA.
The agency would gain powers to request information from directly supervised firms, conduct inspections, investigate breaches, and impose financial penalties. The draft also envisages the authority to restrict services or withdraw authorization where firms do not meet regulatory requirements.
While most crypto service providers would remain under national regulators, ESMA would use guidelines, peer reviews, coordinated investigations, and certain intervention powers to address uneven enforcement across jurisdictions.
The overhaul would also create a full-time ESMA executive board, including a chair and five independent members, to handle operational and company-specific decisions. National regulators would continue participating in broader policy and supervisory coordination.
The Council envisages a two-year transition in which joint teams transfer information, operational responsibilities and expertise to ESMA. Existing MiCA licenses for companies brought under direct supervision would remain valid, avoiding the automatic need to seek new authorization.
The proposed structure would bring greater supervisory scrutiny to a small group of large firms while leaving the majority of the market within the current national model. The decisive questions now concern the final thresholds, ESMA's available resources, and how providers near the boundary are treated.
The Council must formally adopt its negotiating position before talks can begin once the European Parliament establishes its own. Those negotiations will determine how many crypto companies ultimately move from national to EU-level supervision and when the transfer can begin.

items.content:
微软将加大自研AI芯片使用，Maia 300预计2027年投产

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，微软计划逐步提高自研 AI 芯片在数据中心的使用比例，以降低对英伟达 GPU 的依赖。微软表示，未来将主要依靠自研 Maia 芯片架构处理 AI 模型请求，并计划在 Maia 系列芯片上部署数吉瓦级算力。

微软周一公布第三代 AI 加速芯片 Maia 300，预计于 2027 年投产。每个数据中心机架可搭载 96 颗 Maia 300 芯片，是上一代 Maia 200 的两倍；与 GPU 相比，其每机架 AI Token 处理量最高可达 7 倍，每兆瓦可处理的 Token 数量提升约 40%。

微软称，Maia 300 有望提升 AI 服务性能并降低数据中心运营成本。Evercore ISI 分析师预计，截至 2027 年第一季度，Maia 芯片将占微软 AI 芯片支出的约 10%。

不过，英伟达仍将是微软 AI 基础设施的重要供应商。微软表示，模型训练仍将使用英伟达和 AMD 芯片。与谷歌 TPU、亚马逊 Trainium 等产品不同，微软自研加速芯片目前尚未向其他企业开放租用。

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，摩根士丹利首席美股策略师 Mike Wilson 表示，美国 10 年期国债收益率自 2 月以来已上涨约 120 个基点，叠加美元走强、油价高企，金融条件明显收紧，债券市场正在提前完成部分原本需要美联储通过加息实现的紧缩任务。若这一过程足以抑制经济需求，美联储未来可能无需进一步加息。

items.title: Ledger spyware scare spreads beyond Southeast Asia
items.content:
Ledger spyware scare spreads beyond Southeast Asia
More examples of Ledger wallets being tampered with and fitted with physical spyware have allegedly been identified across Asia, Europe, and South America.
Ledger users who bought hardware wallets from Malaysia-based reseller CryptoBilis were drained of over $86 million last week.
Former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès discovered that spyware implanted in some Ledger devices was being used to read their screen output. It could record any seed phrase while remaining undetected by Ledger’s Genuine Check security protocol.
Ledger confirmed yesterday that the incident on October 9 affected a “limited” number of devices sold by CryptoBilis.
“We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products,” it said.
More Ledger wallets flagged with spyware
Self-proclaimed semi-professional airdrop farmer “@0xJohannes_” claimed to have unpacked a Ledger device with a spy implant that was bought directly from Ledger’s official German reseller MediaMarkt.
The device did not appear to redirect any funds to an exploiter, with the X user noting, “Either the device didn’t work or they were waiting for a more widespread usage of the comprised devices.”
They also claimed that “there are reported cases in Asia, South America, and now Europe as well.”
Read more: Ledger says Southeast Asia reseller linked to $86M draining
Another X user, “@Us_Chan007,” shared pictures of the interior of a Ledger wallet they bought from official Philippine reseller LazMall.
Karpelès noted this wallet was fitted with an earlier style of spyware in the form of a “manual coil antenna.”
He also helped identify spyware implanted in one of Ledger’s Stax models shared by X user @wentrre, who’d also bought from CryptoBilis.
Read more: Ledger sued for $500M over its many data breaches
Despite these examples, there are also dozens of users dismantling their Ledger devices out of caution only to be told by Karpelès that they’re “clean.”
Former CryptoBilis exec says firm is under new management
At one point this weekend, attention turned to CryptoBilis’ former CEO, Arravind Prabu, who revealed in an exchange on X that the firm was acquired earlier this year, and that he’s stepped down from all operations.
When quizzed about CryptoBilis’ recent Lamborghini and pizza post, he claims that the account is under new management and that former staff signed a confidentiality clause that meant they couldn’t reveal the company was under new ownership.

items.title: Strategy Scoops Up $21.5M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $192M in STRC
items.content:
In brief
- Bitcoin treasury firm Strategy bought 250 BTC for $21.5 million last week, at an average price of $86,194 per coin, bringing its holdings to 848,250 BTC.
- The company also repurchased 1.93 million shares of its STRC preferred stock for $192.4 million.
- Strategy funded the Bitcoin purchase mainly by selling $21 million of MSTR common stock, and holds $5.5 billion in U.S. dollar assets.
Strategy bought 250 BTC last week and spent $192.4 million repurchasing its STRC preferred stock, the company said on Monday.
The Bitcoin treasury firm paid $21.5 million for the coins between October 5 and October 11, an average of $86,194 per Bitcoin including fees, according to its release. It now holds 848,250 BTC, a new record, acquired for a total of $64 billion at an average of $75,444 per coin.
Strategy raised $21 million by selling about 125,000 shares of its MSTR common stock through its at-the-market offering program, and used $500,000 of cash to cover the rest. It sold none of its preferred stock during the week.
The company repurchased 1,932,145 shares of STRC, its variable-rate Stretch preferred stock, leaving $354.8 million available under its program to buy back preferred shares.
Last week, Strategy bought $29 million in Bitcoin and repurchased $176 million of STRC as it posted a $21 billion third-quarter gain.
Strategy's dollar reserves
As of October 11, Strategy held $4.88 billion in a U.S. dollar reserve set aside for preferred dividends and debt interest, and $640.5 million in cash for broader purposes such as buying Bitcoin.
Strategy set up its USD reserve with $1.44 billion, and later established the separate USD cash pot after raising $2 billion by selling MSTR stock.
The company has also proposed that its preferred stock dividends accrue 365 days a year, and has said it could sell up to $1.25 billion of Bitcoin under its digital credit capital framework.
Strategy CEO Phong Le defended selling Bitcoin as the "right trade" in September, weeks before the firm set a new holdings record at the end of the month with a $143 million purchase. Despite the uptick in buying, traders on prediction market Myriad, owned by Decrypt's parent company Dastan, do not expect the firm's holdings to surpass one million BTC by the end of the year, putting just a 5% chance on that outcome.

items.title: Strategy adds 250 Bitcoin as holdings reach 848,250 BTC
items.content:
Strategy adds 250 Bitcoin as holdings reach 848,250 BTC
Michael Saylor’s Strategy said Bitcoin holdings reached 848,250 BTC after its latest purchase, while maintaining a $4.88 billion cash reserve.
Strategy bought 250 Bitcoin for $21.5 million last week, marking a second consecutive weekly decline in purchases as its Bitcoin holdings reached 848,250 BTC.
The company funded $21 million of the purchases through sales of its common stock and the remaining $500,000 with existing cash between Monday and Sunday, according to an announcement published on Strategy’s website.
Strategy also continued repurchasing shares of its STRC preferred stock, spending $192.4 million during the week, up from $176.3 million the previous week.
The company’s Nasdaq-traded common stock, MSTR, was up less than 1% ahead of Monday’s market opening, according to Yahoo Finance. The preferred stock was poised to open at $99.68 a share.
The company said it maintains a $4.88 billion US Reserve to support preferred stock dividends and debt interest payments. Its separate USD Cash balance stood at $640.5 million as of Sunday.
The purchase followed a Sunday post by founder and executive chair Michael Saylor, who signaled another Bitcoin purchase with the message, “There’s always room for more orange.” Strategy typically reports its Bitcoin purchases in filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, which is closed Monday for the Columbus Day holiday.
Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation has slowed in recent months. Its holdings grew just 0.2% during the third quarter, as the company acquired 7,218 BTC while selling 5,553 BTC.

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，沙特能源大臣阿卜杜勒阿齐兹·本·萨勒曼近日表示，沙特计划在未来两至三年内，将绕开霍尔木兹海峡的陆上石油输送能力提升至每日 1000 万桶，以降低对波斯湾航运通道的依赖。

目前，沙特东西输油管道连接东部油田与红海沿岸延布港，设计输送能力为每日 700 万桶。截至 10 月上旬，该管道实际日输送量已升至 580 万桶，其中约 450 万桶用于出口，其余供应西部炼厂。沙特正对沿线泵站进行增压改造，以进一步提升运力。

此外，沙特还计划临时改造现有天然气管道用于原油运输。相关管线调整后可实现每日约 120 万桶的输油能力，后续若增加泵站和压缩机投资，潜在运力有望提升至 300 万桶。沙特方面还在评估油气双用途管网方案，以便根据地缘风险和季节性需求灵活切换运输用途。

此次布局旨在应对霍尔木兹海峡航运受阻及红海航线安全风险，建立更具弹性的原油外运体系。不过，千万桶级陆上输送能力仍处于规划和建设推进阶段，最终能否实现取决于管网改造及配套设施投资。

items.title: HashKey入选巴伦中国价值榜单「中国行业先锋30强」，成唯一上榜数字资产金融服务公司
items.content:
HashKey入选巴伦中国价值榜单「中国行业先锋30强」，成唯一上榜数字资产金融服务公司

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，HashKey Holdings（3887.HK）10 月 12 日宣布，公司入选 2026 巴伦中国价值榜单「中国行业先锋 30 强」（Value Industry Benchmark 30），是本届 30 家入选企业中唯一一家数字资产金融服务公司。

据介绍，该榜单由巴伦中国发起，重点评估企业的资本效率、风险控制、治理透明度及长期基本面，旨在遴选各垂直领域具有行业影响力的标杆企业。

HashKey 表示，此次入选体现了其在数字资产金融服务领域的合规实践、业务布局及全球拓展获得认可。未来，公司将继续完善持牌交易、链上服务和资产管理等业务，推动传统金融资本进入数字资产领域。

items.title: DeepSeek拟领投前腾讯AI科学家创办Winverse AI，投后估值约4亿美元
items.content:
DeepSeek拟领投前腾讯AI科学家创办Winverse AI，投后估值约4亿美元

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，据彭博社报道，DeepSeek 拟领投机器人 AI 初创公司 Winverse AI 的首轮融资，融资规模达数千万美元。交易完成后，Winverse AI 估值预计约为 4 亿美元，美团旗下 Long-Z Investments 等投资方也已承诺参与。不过，交易尚未最终敲定，融资估值及投资方名单仍可能发生变化。

Winverse AI 于 2026 年由前腾讯顶尖科学家胡瀚创立。胡瀚曾担任腾讯视觉语言与具身基础模型团队首席科学家，此前还在微软亚洲研究院、百度工作。

此次投资将成为 DeepSeek 成立以来规模较大的初创企业投资之一，也意味着其业务布局正从基础模型训练拓展至具身智能和机器人等现实应用领域。彭博社此前报道称，DeepSeek 正接近完成至少 800 亿元人民币（约 120 亿美元）的新一轮融资，资金主要用于模型训练和数据中心建设。

items.title: 渣打银行迪拜分行提供RLUSD托管服务，拟接入LMAX交易抵押体系
items.content:
渣打银行迪拜分行提供RLUSD托管服务，拟接入LMAX交易抵押体系

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，渣打银行迪拜分行现已为符合条件的机构客户提供 Ripple 美元稳定币 RLUSD 的托管服务，支持在 XRP Ledger 上发行的 RLUSD。渣打还计划与 Ripple 及机构交易平台 LMAX Group 合作，允许客户将存放在渣打的 RLUSD 作为 LMAX 平台交易的抵押品，无需将稳定币转入交易平台。

渣打表示，相关抵押品安排尚未正式上线，仍需完成文件签署、测试、监管要求及内部审批。该模式将资产托管与交易执行分离，机构客户可在银行持有稳定币的同时，将其用于交易抵押。

今年 1 月，Ripple 已向 LMAX 提供 1.5 亿美元融资，以推动 RLUSD 融入其机构交易基础设施。此次合作若落地，将进一步拓展 RLUSD 在机构交易抵押场景中的应用。

此外，渣打近期也在拓展数字资产托管业务，上周宣布计划在新加坡为机构客户提供部分加密货币、稳定币及代币化现实世界资产的托管服务。

items.title: 泽连斯基指责俄方违反能源停火，敦促特朗普出手落实协议
items.content:
泽连斯基指责俄方违反能源停火，敦促特朗普出手落实协议

BlockBeats 消息，10 月 12 日，乌克兰总统泽连斯基周一指责俄罗斯违反美国总统特朗普宣布的俄乌能源停火安排，称俄军袭击了乌克兰哈尔科夫一座热电厂，并敦促美国采取行动，确保俄罗斯遵守协议。

泽连斯基表示，乌方至今仍未收到能源停火的具体条款，自己也是通过媒体才得知特朗普宣布双方同意停火。他称，过去一周俄军对乌克兰发电和输电设施发动了 200 多次袭击，另有 17 次袭击针对油气设施，并表示乌军周日晚间没有袭击俄罗斯炼油厂。

欧洲方面对停火能否落实持谨慎态度。法国总统马克龙表示，过去 48 小时内未看到俄罗斯遵守能源停火的迹象。欧盟外长周一批准新增近 1600 项针对俄罗斯军工综合体的制裁列名，其中超过一半涉及弹道导弹生产链。

另据路透社援引知情人士报道，美国曾威胁暂停与乌克兰的情报共享，并停止通过相关机制提供武器，以施压乌方停止袭击俄罗斯能源设施。俄罗斯方面尚未就此次停火安排作出回应。
